reasons: The cited paragraphs (Section 13 term/discontinuation and Section 14 termination) contain no transition-assistance, data-return, export-format or deletion-certification mechanic; Section 13 only obliges Client to arrange a replacement name server/hosting environment and confirms ownership of domains and Client Content, which is not a return right. A 'missing' classification is therefore supportable for a hosting agreement.

The inserted paragraph tracks the playbook model language closely (six months' assistance at then-current rates, return within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, then deletion with written certification) and is correctly localized to the parties and the actual data categories (Client Content, Credit Data, other Client data). The legal-retention carve-out is a reasonable, non-prejudicial addition.

The edit is an insertion only \u2014 the existing Section 14 text is untouched \u2014 so it is the smallest change that reaches the preferred position; deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and data-return/transition language is present.
The comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, explains what changed and why (60-day rehosting duty with no data-return right), cites the playbook position and offers the 90-day fallback.
